notes.approach_chosen: Both options combined, with pigment's limits as the single owner. (1) Per layer degrade with a typed loss (the lead's option b) for a stack over pigment's 64: that is the only place a document can lose something, and it is the limit the render plan would refuse anyway (PlanError::EffectLimit), so a bigger stack could not be rendered. (2) The record-validation node budget is sized from the input (option a) inside a documented hard cap, because at pigment's own limit (4096 instances) Folio needs 4096 + one node per record layer and the caller's default is 4096: a document exactly at pigment's limit would otherwise be refused. (3) Whole-import failure only past the per-plan limit, as a typed input error (PsdError::EffectLimit), never as Proposal(..), which stays the mapping-defect family. The caller budget is not raised for anything else: inspect_bytes (document nodes) still uses cfg.budget unchanged
notes.why_not_only_sizing: Sizing alone (no per-layer cap) would admit up to 1024 instances per layer and 8192 layers, i.e. far more than pigment accepts; the render plan would then refuse the document later. The lead's rule was to admit no more than pigment accepts
notes.why_not_only_degrade: Degrading to fit the caller's nodes would make a document that is exactly at pigment's limit lose stacks for a 64-node accounting reason (records + instances = 4160 > 4096), and would tie what imports to the caller's unrelated node setting
notes.caller_budget_semantics: records_budget = Budget { nodes: max(cfg.budget.nodes, records + effect instances), ..cfg.budget }. The caller's input_bytes, payload_bytes, edges and depth apply unchanged. A host that wants a hard node ceiling for effects now sets it through pigment's limits (fixed) rather than Budget::nodes; this is a behaviour change for a host that passed a small nodes value and relied on the record validation to refuse effect-heavy files (before: Proposal(raster_records_rejected))
